principle: Search and context selection are agent decisions. Deterministic runtime exposes authorized search/fetch primitives, candidate blocks, provenance, visibility and resource limits; the model decides what is missing, what query to issue, which evidence matters, whether to reformulate, what to retain and when to stop.

context.select.purpose: Choose useful context for one bounded task and, when supplied candidates are insufficient, request the next authorized search instead of pretending a precomputed context window is semantically complete.
rubric: Treat the supplied memory blocks as mechanically eligible candidates, not as a claim that they are narratively relevant or sufficient.
Decide what the current task actually needs. Select only evidence that helps the immediate reasoning, even when a superficially similar or recent block is available.

If evidence is insufficient and an allowed search capability is supplied, formulate the next focused query yourself. You may broaden, narrow or reformulate based on search_history; do not search merely because a tool exists.
Stop when the current task is sufficiently grounded. Do not compulsively retrieve more context after the evidence is adequate.
Respect story-time and perspective visibility already encoded in the packet. Selection never upgrades plan, proposal, review, research or derived memory into Accepted Canon.
Pinned blocks are execution constraints, not proof of semantic importance. Preserve them in selected_ids unless the packet itself is invalid, but do not infer meaning from pinning.
Return selected ids plus either enough or search_more. The runtime may enforce capability/resource bounds but must not rewrite your semantic relevance decision.

corpus.discovery_plan.purpose: Plan bounded evidence searches for a supplied Corpus/research gap. Query design, contrast strategy and stopping logic are semantic work; authorization and rights remain runtime responsibilities.
rubric: Use the supplied research gap, source constraints and declared capability vocabulary.
Design focused searches that can answer the research question with evidence and meaningful counterexamples or contrasts when useful.
Prefer primary, official, publisher, library or research sources when the source constraints request them.
Do not select an unavailable/unauthorized channel and do not claim channel availability merely because you named it.
Do not search in order to imitate a named living author or build a named-author style profile.
Return search intent only. Discovery, rights classification, ingestion and promotion happen through their own authority paths.
